Dated this the 31st day of May, 2024 This is an application for anticipatory bail filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure by accused Nos.1 to 4 in Crime No.413/2024 of Cantonment Police Station, Thiruvananthapuram.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Perused the relevant documents.

3. The prosecution case is that the 1st accused married the defacto complainant on 14.08.2023 as Nibin Jayaraj vs State Of Kerala on 31 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12763563/
1 per religious ceremonies at Chappath St.Mary's Auditorium and they jointly stayed at the matrimonial home.

sentences.text: The allegation is that during the stay, the accused herein subjected her to mental and physical cruelty, demanding more dowry.
On this premise, the prosecution alleges commission of offences punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that no serious allegations could be gathered from the prosecution materials and therefore, arrest and custodial interrogation of the petitioners are not necessary and the petitioners are ready to co-operate with the investigation.

5. Although the learned Public Prosecutor opposed bail, on perusal of prosecution records, general allegations of cruelty during stay of the couples at the matrimonial home is the crux of the dispute.
Therefore, investigation is possible even without custodial interrogation.
6. Having considered the factual matrix of the case in the above line, I am of the view that the petitioners deserve anticipatory bail.
Thus, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioners on anticipatory bail, with direction to the petitioners to co-operate with the investigation.
Therefore, this petition stands allowed.

The petitioners are enlarged on anticipatory bail on the following conditions:
i.
The petitioners shall surrender before the Investigating Officer within ten days from today and on such surrender, the Investigating Officer can question the petitioners and record their statement.
In the event of their arrest, the Investigating Officer shall produce the petitioners before the Jurisdictional Court on the date of arrest itself.

ii. On such production, Jurisdictional Court shall release the petitioners on bail, on executing bond for Rs.30,000/- (Rupees thirty thousand) each by themselves and by two solvent sureties, each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the Jurisdictional Court.
iii. The petitioners shall co-operate with investigation and shall be made available for interrogation and for the purpose of investigation, as and when the Investigating Officer directs so.
iv. The petitioners shall not, intimidate the witnesses or interfere with the investigation in any manner.
v. The petitioners shall not commit any offence during the currency of this bail and any such involvement is a reason to cancel the bail hereby granted.
